meta.name: Step by step
meta.about: Three paths through HAX in order: how a page loads (index.html, the site builder tag, site.json, the theme, the page, then only the elements it uses), how a page is added, and how a site is restructured with the outline designer in one atomic save. Solid arrows are the order; dotted lines are what each step touches.

flows.desc: Three things that happen in HAX, in order. Play a path and the steps light up one at a time; each step points at the parts of the ecosystem it touches.

fl_load.desc: From the request to a rendered page: the site builder tag, site.json, the theme, the page HTML, then the elements the page uses, lazily.

l1.desc: The browser asks for a URL. HAXcms on PHP or Node.js, a static host or a HAX11ty build answers with the site's index.html.

l2.desc: A small page: an import map, a preload of wc-registry.json and base.css, the web app manifest, the <haxcms-site-builder file="site.json?hash"> tag already in the markup, then build-haxcms.js and build.js.

l3.desc: Detects module support, sets up WCAutoload and loads the haxcms-site-builder module. Nothing else is loaded yet.

l4.desc: haxcms-site-builder upgrades and fetches its file attribute: site.json, the JSON Outline Schema manifest. haxcms-site-store holds it for everything else.

l5.desc: From manifest.metadata.theme, the builder imports the theme element by path, waits for customElements.whenDefined, and stamps it. The theme draws menu, breadcrumb and regions from the store.

l6.desc: The router turns the URL slug into the active item. The builder fetches that item's location, pages/<id>/index.html, with the build timestamp; a missing page shows the 404.

l7.desc: The HTML is placed in the theme's content slot and an active-item event fires, so menus, previous and next, and xAPI listeners update.

l8.desc: wc-autoload watches the DOM for tags that are not defined, looks each up in wc-registry.json and imports its module. Only the elements this page uses are loaded, and they upgrade in place.

l9.desc: The service worker registers for offline use, search is ready at x/search, and if you are logged in the editor UI loads and the registry graph warms the editor's own elements.

fl_add.desc: From logging in to a new page readers can see.

a1.desc: POST session login. haxcms-site-editor-ui appears: the top bar with Add page, Edit, Outline designer and the dashboard.

a2.desc: Choose Add page from the top bar, or ask Merlin. Pick a title, where it goes, and what to start from: blank, a template, a clone, or an imported file.

a3.desc: POST /x/api/v1/items. The backend writes pages/<id>/index.html and appends the item (id, parent, order, slug, location) to site.json.

a4.desc: haxcms-site-store refreshes the manifest; menus and breadcrumbs show the page and the router moves to its slug.

a5.desc: Edit mode opens hax-body with the blocks the app store allows for this site. Type / for Merlin's slash commands, drop a file or paste a link to import.

a6.desc: PATCH /x/api/v1/content/{id} saves the HTML to pages/<id>/index.html; PATCH /x/api/v1/items/{id} saves title, published state and metadata to site.json. Git keeps a revision.

a7.desc: The page renders through the same load path as every other page; sitemap, search index and feeds regenerate.

fl_outline.desc: Many changes to a site's structure, staged in one view and saved in one operation.

o1.desc: From the top bar or the dashboard. outline-designer loads the items from the store's manifest.
o1.note: Part of: Restructure with the outline designer

o2.desc: Drag to reorder, indent or outdent to nest, rename, add, duplicate, delete, lock, publish or unpublish. Every change is staged locally as a diff; nothing is written yet.
o2.note: Part of: Restructure with the outline designer

o3.desc: PATCH /x/api/v1/site/outline: the whole set of operations in one atomic call. The backend validates it, writes site.json, and creates or removes page files as needed. Both backends behave identically.
o3.note: Part of: Restructure with the outline designer

o4.desc: The store refreshes the manifest; menus, breadcrumbs, previous and next, the sitemap and search follow the new structure.
o4.note: Part of: Restructure with the outline designer

o5.desc: Bulk structure changes are mission critical, so outline-designer and saveOutline are covered by end-to-end and conformance tests; save and failure behavior cannot change from a data-model change.
o5.note: Part of: Restructure with the outline designer

tours.label: A page loads
tours.message: From the request to a rendered page: the site builder tag, site.json, the theme, the page HTML, then the elements the page uses, lazily.

scenes.caption: 1. Request. The browser asks for a URL. HAXcms on PHP or Node.js, a static host or a HAX11ty build answers with the site's index.html.

2. index.html. A small page: an import map, a preload of wc-registry.json and base.css, the web app manifest, the <haxcms-site-builder file="site.json?hash"> tag already in the markup, then build-haxcms.js and build.js.
3. build.js boots. Detects module support, sets up WCAutoload and loads the haxcms-site-builder module. Nothing else is loaded yet.
4. site.json. haxcms-site-builder upgrades and fetches its file attribute: site.json, the JSON Outline Schema manifest. haxcms-site-store holds it for everything else.

5. The theme. From manifest.metadata.theme, the builder imports the theme element by path, waits for customElements.whenDefined, and stamps it. The theme draws menu, breadcrumb and regions from the store.
6. Route to a page. The router turns the URL slug into the active item. The builder fetches that item's location, pages/<id>/index.html, with the build timestamp; a missing page shows the 404.
7. Content into the theme. The HTML is placed in the theme's content slot and an active-item event fires, so menus, previous and next, and xAPI listeners update.

8. Elements load lazily. wc-autoload watches the DOM for tags that are not defined, looks each up in wc-registry.json and imports its module. Only the elements this page uses are loaded, and they upgrade in place.
9. After render. The service worker registers for offline use, search is ready at x/search, and if you are logged in the editor UI loads and the registry graph warms the editor's own elements.
A page loads: the whole path.

tours.label: Add a page
tours.message: From logging in to a new page readers can see.

scenes.caption: 1. Log in. POST session login. haxcms-site-editor-ui appears: the top bar with Add page, Edit, Outline designer and the dashboard.
2. Add page. Choose Add page from the top bar, or ask Merlin. Pick a title, where it goes, and what to start from: blank, a template, a clone, or an imported file.
3. The item is created. POST /x/api/v1/items. The backend writes pages/<id>/index.html and appends the item (id, parent, order, slug, location) to site.json.
4. The store updates. haxcms-site-store refreshes the manifest; menus and breadcrumbs show the page and the router moves to its slug.
5. Write. Edit mode opens hax-body with the blocks the app store allows for this site. Type / for Merlin's slash commands, drop a file or paste a link to import.
6. Save. PATCH /x/api/v1/content/{id} saves the HTML to pages/<id>/index.html; PATCH /x/api/v1/items/{id} saves title, published state and metadata to site.json. Git keeps a revision.
7. Readers see it. The page renders through the same load path as every other page; sitemap, search index and feeds regenerate.
Add a page: the whole path.

tours.label: Restructure with the outline designer
tours.message: Many changes to a site's structure, staged in one view and saved in one operation.

scenes.caption: 1. Open the outline designer. From the top bar or the dashboard. outline-designer loads the items from the store's manifest.
2. Stage changes. Drag to reorder, indent or outdent to nest, rename, add, duplicate, delete, lock, publish or unpublish. Every change is staged locally as a diff; nothing is written yet.

3. Save once. PATCH /x/api/v1/site/outline: the whole set of operations in one atomic call. The backend validates it, writes site.json, and creates or removes page files as needed. Both backends behave identically.
4. Everything follows. The store refreshes the manifest; menus, breadcrumbs, previous and next, the sitemap and search follow the new structure.

5. Why it is guarded. Bulk structure changes are mission critical, so outline-designer and saveOutline are covered by end-to-end and conformance tests; save and failure behavior cannot change from a data-model change.
Restructure with the outline designer: the whole path.
